lesson.title: Review Day: Newton's Laws of Motion
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: This week you mastered all three of Newton's laws. Let's review it all!

Quick review: the First Law is inertia (Day 1). The Second Law is F=ma (Day 2). The Third Law is equal-and-opposite action-reaction pairs (Day 3). You saw all three work together in a rocket launch (Day 4). A 3 kg object experiences a net force of 15 N. Find its acceleration, and explain which of Newton's three laws is most directly demonstrated by this calculation.
Great work this week — you mastered all three of Newton's laws! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review all three of Newton's laws
Correctly calculate acceleration and identify which law it demonstrates
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child solve the new F=ma problem and identify the law.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of Newton's laws mastery!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the law the child found hardest this week (often the Third Law) rather than requiring all three equally
Ready for more: ask the child to design their own simple real-world example demonstrating all three laws, like this week's rocket example
This is a good checkpoint to note which of Newton's three laws needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: a = F/m = 15/3 = 5 m/s². This calculation directly demonstrates Newton's Second Law (F=ma), which connects a net force and mass to a resulting acceleration.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's NGSS Grade 9-12 Newton's-laws standard (HS-PS2-1) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
